Let \(t=\alpha\lambda\). Since \(x_{-1}=x_0\), the first momentum term is zero, so

\[
x_1=(1-\alpha\lambda)x_0=(1-t)x_0.
\]

Then

\[
x_2=(1-t)x_1+\beta(x_1-x_0)
=\left((1-t)^2-\beta t\right)x_0.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{x_2}{x_0}=p(t),\qquad
p(t)=t^2-(2+\beta)t+1,
\]

and \(t\in[\alpha,9\alpha]\). Put \(c=2+\beta\ge2\), so we minimize

\[
\max_{t\in[\alpha,9\alpha]} |t^2-ct+1|.
\]

For any \(\alpha>0\), evaluate \(p\) at the three points

\[
\alpha,\quad 5\alpha,\quad 9\alpha.
\]

By Lagrange interpolation at \(t=0\),

\[
p(0)=\frac{45p(\alpha)-18p(5\alpha)+5p(9\alpha)}{32}.
\]

Since \(p(0)=1\), if \(M=\max_{t\in[\alpha,9\alpha]}|p(t)|\), then

\[
1\le \frac{45M+18M+5M}{32}
=\frac{68M}{32},
\]

so

\[
M\ge \frac{8}{17}.
\]

Therefore \(R(\alpha,\beta)\ge 8/17\) for every admissible \((\alpha,\beta)\).

Now choose equality signs:

\[
p(\alpha)=\frac8{17},\qquad
p(5\alpha)=-\frac8{17},\qquad
p(9\alpha)=\frac8{17}.
\]

The second difference gives

\[
p(\alpha)-2p(5\alpha)+p(9\alpha)=32\alpha^2,
\]

so

\[
\frac{32}{17}=32\alpha^2
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\alpha=\frac1{\sqrt{17}}.
\]

Also \(p(\alpha)=p(9\alpha)\) gives

\[
c=10\alpha=\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}}.
\]

Thus

\[
\beta=c-2=\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}}-2\ge0.
\]

For these parameters,

\[
p(t)=t^2-\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}}t+1.
\]

On \(\left[\frac1{\sqrt{17}},\frac9{\sqrt{17}}\right]\), its endpoint values are \(8/17\), and its vertex is at \(t=5/\sqrt{17}\), where the value is \(-8/17\). Hence the maximum absolute value is exactly \(8/17\).

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac8{17},\left(\frac1{\sqrt{17}},\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}}-2\right)\right)}
\]
